answers.explanation: Several layer 3 addresses, one layer 2 address.
Both addresses belong to the same NIC, so both resolve to the same MAC.
ip addr add, with the address, prefix, and interface. On macOS: sudo ifconfig en0 alias 192.168.1.15 netmask 255.255.255.0 up.
ifconfig's alias keyword adds an address rather than replacing the main one.
Command-line changes are lost on reboot. For a permanent alias, use the OS's configuration files, such as netplan or /etc/network/interfaces on Ubuntu.
DHCP gives one address per interface. Aliases are configured statically.
Add the new address alongside the old, move everyone over, then remove the old one.
Different networks normally talk through a router. An alias lets this one host reach both directly.
